stimuli.title: Hema, Gita, Deepa, Charu, Bina, Uma, Esha, Sana occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.

• Deepa and Sana occupy flats with different letters.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some coins are cards. All cards are tokens. No tokens is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are tokens.
II. Some cards are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are cards. Some cards are tokens. All tokens are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are cheques.
II. No cards is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No coins is a cards. Some cards are tokens. All tokens are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are cheques.
II. Some cheques are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are cards. All cards are tokens. No tokens is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are not cards.
II. No cards is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: W > R < U > V < S.
Conclusions: I. R > V   II. W ≥ U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: T < W > P < Q > S.
Conclusions: I. W ≤ S   II. S < W.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth rural secure = mi ze re
growth banking savings = ze ni su
rural banking digital = su vo mi
secure savings digital = ni vo re
growth rural digital = ze vo mi
What is the code for “digital”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = ze, rural = mi, secure = re, banking = su, savings = ni, digital = vo.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 81 km east, turns right and walks 168 km, then turns right and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 182. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 70 km along the initial direction and 168 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(70² + 168²) = 182 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 30 km west, turns right and walks 32 km, then turns right and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 24 km along the initial direction and 32 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 23 km south, turns right and walks 30 km, then turns right and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 16 km along the initial direction and 30 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 km.

questions.stem: G is the mother of E. A is the son of E. H is the father of E. How is A related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. H is a parent of E, and A is E’s son. Hence A is H’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the brother of E. E is the mother of B. D is the father of F and E. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. F is the brother of B’s mother E. Therefore F is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of G. G is the father of D. E is the son of D. H is the sister of G. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of D, and D is E’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 13th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New front rank = 13+3 = 16. Back rank = 60 − 16 + 1 = 45.

questions.stem: In a queue of 35 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 13. New front rank = 19+4 = 23. Back rank = 35 − 23 + 1 = 13.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1600. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2389.33. Selling price = 1600 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 2389.33.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 24 days and B in 36 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 19. Use 72 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 72 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 252 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 16 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹17000 for 12 months. B invests ₹34000 for 7 months. Total profit is ₹62400. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 33600. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 14. B’s share = total × 14/(26) = 33600.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹17000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 382.5. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 17000 × (15/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 60 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 12. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 12.

questions.stem: The average of 31 numbers is 68. One number, 80, is replaced and the average rises by 4. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 204. Total increases by 31 × 4. New number = 80 + 124.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 6 years, their combined age will be 80 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 12 = 80; x = 17, so father = 51.
